disease_label_per_paper: Myeloma CAR-T cytokine release syndrome treated with tocilizumab, vasopressors, and ICU monitoring
presentation_summary: IgA kappa myeloma after 12 prior lines of therapy admitted for anti-BCMA CAR-T therapy.
Fever and chills developed 6 hours after infusion with initially normal BP, oxygen saturation and mental status.
On day 2 he developed tachycardia, hypotension to 86/39 mmHg, high CRP and ferritin >22000, requiring ICU transfer, tocilizumab and norepinephrine.
Blood cultures had no growth; fever resolved by day 8 and he was discharged home on day 16.

risk_context.source_text_value: received 12 lines of therapy and two autologous stem cell transplants

clinical_timeline.event: Fever 100.4 F and chills 6 hours after CAR-T infusion; started empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics.
Fever up to 104.2 F; hemodynamically and neurologically stable; CRP rose from 21.5 to 50.
Tachycardia and BP 86/39 mmHg; ICU transfer, tocilizumab 4 mg/kg, norepinephrine 10 mcg/hr; CRP 201 and ferritin >22000.
Fever 101.8 F but titrated off vasopressor support.
Transferred out of ICU; blood cultures with no growth.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Paper graded the episode as CRS grade 3
Longitudinal cytokine profiling mirrored the clinical CRS course
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: elevated IL-2, IFN-gamma, IL-6, IL-10, IL-18 and sIL-2RA mirrored the clinical course of CRS

outcome.short_term: Off vasopressors by day 4, transferred out of ICU day 5, fever resolved day 8.
